content.overview: Section 230 is the Tribunal scheme jurisdiction for compromises with creditors or members.
content.glance: Section 230 is the Tribunal scheme jurisdiction for compromises with creditors or members.
content.study: Compromises and arrangements. Section 230 is the Tribunal scheme jurisdiction for compromises with creditors or members. The section applies only to the persons, companies, and transactions it names. A filing, approval, or penalty arises only where the section or a rule under it says so. It does not create a power that is reserved to another section or to the Tribunal. Not a verified closure.

sections.body: Section 230 is the Tribunal scheme jurisdiction for compromises with creditors or members.

sections.heading: Explanation
sections.body: Notice, disclosure, majority in number and three-fourths in value, and sanction are mandatory. Takeover offers have extra conditions. The order is filed and then binds dissenting members of the class.
